mainTopic: Whom מר זוטרא's ruling rejects, and how mixing 'gift' and 'inheritance' wording works when a dying man divides his property
overview: The גמרא first asks whose opinion מר זוטרא's ruling for רבי אבא is meant to reject. It finds that the ruling rejects רבי יוחנן's view about testifying to a בכור and מר בר רב אשי's objection. Next it turns to the משנה about a שכיב מרע who divides his property. רב דימי, in the name of רבי יוחנן, explains what a gift 'at the beginning, end, and middle' sounds like. He limits this to one person and one field, while רבי אלעזר allows it even when only the person or only the field is shared. רבין reports a different version of רבי יוחנן that allows even two people and two fields. When אביי objects, רבין answers that the two reporters hold different traditions of רבי יוחנן's view, and ריש לקיש adds his own condition. The sages of בבל split the same way: רב המנונא, רב נחמן and רב ששת. רב ששת then begins quoting a ברייתא about weekly money for children as his proof, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Which opinion does מר זוטרא's ruling reject? Three options fail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests three possible targets of מר זוטרא's ruling for רבי אבא, and each one fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ruling is meant to reject רבא, that makes no sense, because רבא only adds to רבי אבא. If it is meant to reject מר בר רב אשי, we already know the הלכה is not like him. If it is meant to reject שמואל, רב ששת and רב פפא, their views were already disproved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to work out whose opinion מר זוטרא meant to push aside when he said the הלכה follows רבי אבא. It tries three candidates and knocks each one down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling of הלכה is only needed if it rejects someone who disagrees. רבא does not disagree with רבי אבא; he goes further. מר בר רב אשי's view and the view of שמואל, רב ששת and רב פפא were already rejected earlier, so a new ruling against them would add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude; to reject another opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Each 'אי' line is not a real proposal. It is a possibility the גמרא raises only so it can show why it cannot be right.

phrases.english: If it is to exclude the view of Rava
phrases.notes: "It" means מר זוטרא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אבא, which was stated just before this.

phrases.english: he is adding!
If it is to exclude that of Mar bar Rav Ashi

phrases.aramaic: – לֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי!
phrases.english: the halakha is not in accordance with Mar bar Rav Ashi!
If it is to exclude the view of Shmuel
and Rav Sheshet and Rav Pappa
they were already refuted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of מר זוטרא's ruling for רבי אבא
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that מר זוטרא's ruling rejects רבא, מר בר רב אשי, or שמואל, רב ששת and רב פפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling must reject a real, still-standing opposing view, and none of these qualifies

steps.title: The ruling rejects רבי יוחנן and מר בר רב אשי's objection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that מר זוטרא's ruling is aimed against רבי יוחנן and against מר בר רב אשי's objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ruling is meant to reject רבי יוחנן's view, and to reject the strong objection of מר בר רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the three options in step 1 failed, the גמרא gives the real answer: the ruling pushes aside רבי יוחנן's view and מר בר רב אשי's objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן held that a person cannot testify that a particular son is his בכור, so the ruling teaches that we do not follow him. מר בר רב אשי had objected to רבי אבא's rule in the case where a borrower admits part of a claim and witnesses say he paid everything. The ruling teaches that despite that objection, the borrower does not take a שבועה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 1. There, מר בר רב אשי's own ruling was set aside. Here, what is rejected is his objection against רבי אבא, which is a different statement.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי אבא. This rejects רבי יוחנן's view on testifying about a בכור and מר בר רב אשי's objection about the borrower's שבועה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to exclude the view of Rabbi Yoḥanan
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's view that a person cannot testify that a certain son is his בכור.

phrases.english: and the strong objection of Mar bar Rav Ashi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 1 by naming the real targets of the ruling
steps.terutzResolutionType: Names different targets for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the ruling was aimed at רבא, מר בר רב אשי's own ruling, or שמואל, רב ששת and רב פפא
steps.terutzMaskana: It rejects רבי יוחנן's view and מר בר רב אשי's objection

steps.title: What does a gift at the beginning, middle, or end look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a dying man who divides his property and asks what the three wordings mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who divides his property by spoken word, giving more to one son and less to another, and so on. What is a case of 'gift at the beginning'? What is 'in the middle'? What is 'at the end'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה and asks for examples of the three wordings the משנה mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that ירושה language alone cannot change the תורה's shares, but מתנה language can. It also says that if the gift wording appears at the beginning, middle or end, the gift stands. The גמרא wants to know exactly what those three phrasings sound like.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what does it look like?

phrases.english: One who divides his property orally
phrases.notes: This is someone on his deathbed (a שכיב מרע), whose spoken words are enough without a written deed.

phrases.english: increased for one and decreased for one, etc.
What is the case of a gift at the beginning?
What is the case of in the middle?
What is the case of at the end?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next part of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Concrete wordings for a gift at the beginning, middle, and end

steps.title: רב דימי gives the three wordings in the name of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains each case by where the word 'given' appears next to the word 'inherit'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'Let such a field be given to so-and-so, and he will inherit it' is a gift at the beginning. 'He will inherit it, and let it be given to him' is a gift at the end. 'He will inherit it, and let it be given to him, and he will inherit it' is a gift in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 3. The position of the gift word (תנתן) among the inheritance words decides whether it is 'beginning,' 'end,' or 'middle.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the man uses both ירושה language and מתנה language. Because the gift word is present somewhere, the transfer works as a מתנה, whether that word comes first, last, or between two inheritance words.

keyTerms.meaning: when (he) came, from ארץ ישראל to בבל
and he will inherit it (inheritance language)

steps.confusionAlert: The order here is beginning, end, then middle, not the order the question used. Watch where the word תנתן sits in each quote.
steps.whatToRemember: Gift language anywhere in the statement, at the start, the end, or between inheritance words, makes the deathbed transfer work as a מתנה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
"Let such-and-such field be given to so-and-so, and he will inherit it"
this is a gift at the beginning.
"And he will inherit it, and let it be given to him"
this is a gift at the end.
"He will inherit it, and let it be given to him, and he will inherit it"
this is a gift in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Beginning: gift word before 'inherit'. End: gift word after 'inherit'. Middle: gift word between two 'inherit's.

steps.title: The ruling works only with one person and one field
steps.stepSummary: The 'give' wording rescues the 'inherit' wording only when both are said about the same person and the same field.
steps.simpleTranslation: This only works with one person and one field. But with one person and two fields, or one field and two people, it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי, still quoting רבי יוחנן, sets a limit on the rule from the previous step. Mixing 'give' and 'inherit' only helps when both words are said about the same person and the same field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 we learned that the word 'given' next to 'inherit' can make the inheritance work. Now we learn the limit. If either the person or the field changes, the two phrases are no longer tied together, so the 'inherit' part fails and only the 'give' part takes effect.

phrases.english: And this is specifically with one person and one field;
but with one person and two fields,

phrases.aramaic: שָׂדֶה אַחַת וּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם – לֹא.
phrases.english: or one field and two people — no.
phrases.notes: 'No' means the 'inherit' part does not work. Only the part said as a gift takes effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the explanation given in step 4 to the case of one person and one field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixing 'give' with 'inherit' works only when one person and one field are involved.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר widens the rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the rule works even if only the person or only the field is shared. It fails only with two people and two fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: even one person and two fields, or one field and two people, it works. But with two fields and two people, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with the limit in step 5. He allows the rule to work in more cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, one shared link is enough to tie the two phrases together, either the same person or the same field. Only when nothing is shared, meaning two people and two fields, are the phrases fully separate, so the 'inherit' part fails.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees here and allows more cases

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the four cases straight. 1 person + 1 field: everyone agrees it works. 1 person + 2 fields, or 1 field + 2 people: רבי אלעזר says it works. 2 people + 2 fields: according to this teaching, it does not work.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Even one person and two fields,
or one field and two people [it works];

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּשְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת וּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם – לֹא.
phrases.english: but with two fields and two people — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אָדָם אֶחָד וּשְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the limit in step 5 and extends the rule to cases where one element is shared.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule works if either the person or the field is shared. It fails only with two people and two fields.

steps.title: רבין's report: a dispute about two people and two fields
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that in a case of two people and two fields, רבי יוחנן says the person acquires and רבי אלעזר says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: if someone says 'Let field A be given to ראובן, and let שמעון inherit field B,' רבי יוחנן says שמעון acquires it, and רבי אלעזר says he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין brings a new report from ארץ ישראל. It is about the case with two different people and two different fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this report רבי יוחנן says the inheritance works even with two people and two fields. That looks like the opposite of the limit we just learned in his name in step 5. רבי אלעזר says it does not work, which matches his own view in step 6. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
"Let such-and-such field be given to so-and-so,
and let so-and-so inherit such-and-such field" —
phrases.notes: Here the second 'so-and-so' and 'such-and-such' are a different person and a different field. That makes it two people and two fields.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he acquired,
Rabbi Elazar says: he did not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new tradition about the two-people-two-fields case, which seems to clash with step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people and two fields: רבי יוחנן says the person acquires; רבי אלעזר says he does not.

steps.title: אביי shows that רבי אלעזר's two statements fit together
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבין that his report solved one problem and created another. He first shows that רבי אלעזר is consistent, which sets up the real difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבין: you made one thing easier for us and one thing harder! Granted, רבי אלעזר does not contradict himself. In one place he speaks about one person and two fields, and in the other about two people and two fields.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins a challenge against רבין's report. He first clears away the easy part, that רבי אלעזר is consistent, which sets up the hard question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said 'it works' in step 6 and 'he did not acquire' in step 7. That looks like a contradiction, but it is not. Step 6 was about one person and two fields, and step 7 is about two people and two fields. The word 'granted' (בשלמא) tells us that a real problem is about to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: You made it easier for us
You made it harder for us
Granted (this part is fine, but the next part is a problem)
Here... there (each source is talking about a different case)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the full question yet. אביי is only showing what is not a problem. The real difficulty, about רבי יוחנן, comes right after.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Ravin:
You made one thing easier for us,
and you made one thing harder for us!
Granted, Rabbi Elazar against Rabbi Elazar
is not difficult —
here it is one person and two fields,
phrases.notes: 'Here' points back to רבי אלעזר's statement in step 6.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם וּשְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת;
phrases.english: there it is two people and two fields;
phrases.notes: This points to רבין's report in step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבִין: אַנְחֵתְתְּ לַן חֲדָא, וְאַתְקֵפְתְּ לַן חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבין's report by checking it against the earlier statements.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's report, checked against the earlier statements of רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי first clears רבי אלעזר of contradiction by pointing out that the two statements cover different cases. This sets up the difficulty about רבי יוחנן, which comes next.

steps.title: The two reports of רבי יוחנן contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that רבין's report of רבי יוחנן clashes with רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן's statement against רבי יוחנן's statement is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the real problem אביי was building up to. רבי יוחנן seems to say two opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי reported that רבי יוחנן allows the 'give' wording to help only with one person and one field. רבין reported that רבי יוחנן allows it even with two people and two fields. Both cannot be what רבי יוחנן held.

keyTerms.meaning: against (the other statement of) רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: But the statement of רבי יוחנן
against the statement of רבי יוחנן is a difficulty!
phrases.notes: Step 5 (רב דימי) has רבי יוחנן requiring the same person and field. Step 7 (רבין) has him allowing two people and two fields.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge אביי started in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two reports of רבי יוחנן's view (רב דימי's and רבין's)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One sage cannot hold both that the rule works only for one person and one field and that it works even for two people and two fields.

steps.title: Two different traditions about רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבין answers that he and רב דימי are each passing on a different tradition of what רבי יוחנן said.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are אמוראים, and they argue about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין answers אביי. רבי יוחנן did not contradict himself. The reporters received different versions of his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer moves the argument from רבי יוחנן to the people quoting him. רב דימי and רבין each faithfully report what they heard, and their traditions differ. So there is no real self-contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: they are אמוראים (sages of the גמרא)
according to, with regard to the view of

phrases.english: They are אמוראים
and they differ about the view of רבי יוחנן.
phrases.notes: He means that רב דימי and רבין each carry their own tradition of what רבי יוחנן held.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among the people quoting the sage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said two opposite things.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן said one thing. רב דימי and רבין received different traditions of it.

steps.title: ריש לקיש requires everything to be spelled out
steps.stepSummary: With two people and two fields, ריש לקיש says the gift works only if the person names everyone, every field, and uses both 'give' and 'inherit'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש says: he does not acquire unless the giver says: 'So-and-so and so-and-so will inherit such-and-such field and such-and-such field, which I have given them as a gift, and they will inherit them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבין continues his report and adds ריש לקיש's view on the case of two people and two fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said this case does not work. רבין's version of רבי יוחנן says it does. ריש לקיש takes a middle path: it can work, but only if the 'give' and 'inherit' wording covers both people and both fields together.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, the study partner of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: And ריש לקיש says,
he does not acquire unless the giver says:
phrases.notes: This is still רבין's report, about two people and two fields.

phrases.english: 'So-and-so and so-and-so will inherit
such-and-such field and such-and-such field
which I have given them as a gift,
and they will inherit them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר לֹא קָנָה עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third view to רבין's report on the case of two people and two fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two people and two fields, the transfer works only when both names, both fields, and both 'give' and 'inherit' are said together.

steps.title: רב המנונא limits the rule to one person and one field
steps.stepSummary: The sages of בבל argue about the same question. רב המנונא says the rule works only with one person and one field.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute. רב המנונא said: They taught this only about one person and one field. But one person and two fields, or one field and two people, does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the sages of בבל argue about the same thing. It begins with the strictest view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא matches רב דימי's version of רבי יוחנן. If either the person or the field changes, the 'give' wording no longer rescues the 'inherit' wording.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a matter of dispute
רב המנונא, a sage of בבל

phrases.english: It is a matter of dispute:
phrases.notes: The sages of בבל argue about the same question as the sages of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: רב המנונא said:
They taught this only about
one person and one field;
but one person and two fields,

phrases.aramaic: שָׂדֶה אַחַת וּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם – לֹא.
phrases.english: or one field and two people, does not work.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sages of ארץ ישראל to the same dispute among the sages of בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'give' wording helps only when it is the same person and the same field.

steps.title: רב נחמן allows one shared detail
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the rule works if either the person or the field is shared. It fails only with two people and two fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: Even one person and two fields, or one field and two people, works. But two fields and two people does not.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the middle view in the dispute in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן matches רבי אלעזר's view from step 6. One shared link, either the person or the field, is enough to connect the 'give' wording to the 'inherit' wording.

keyTerms.meaning: רב נחמן, a sage of בבל

phrases.english: And רב נחמן said:
Even one person and two fields,
or one field and two people, works;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת וּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם – לֹא.
phrases.english: but two fields and two people does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ אָדָם אֶחָד וּשְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more lenient view than רב המנונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It works if the person or the field is shared. It fails only with two people and two fields.

steps.title: רב ששת allows even two people and two fields
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the rule works even with two people and two fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: Even two fields and two people works.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the most lenient view, and it closes the three-level dispute in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת matches רבין's version of רבי יוחנן. The 'give' wording can rescue the 'inherit' wording even when nothing is shared.

keyTerms.meaning: רב ששת, a sage of בבל

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. Only the same person and same field works (רב המנונא, like רב דימי's version of רבי יוחנן). One shared detail is enough (רב נחמן, like רבי אלעזר). Even two people and two fields works (רב ששת, like רבין's version of רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: רב ששת begins his proof from a ברייתא about weekly money for children
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks where he learns his view and quotes a ברייתא. A father says to give his children a shekel a week. If they need a סלע, they get a סלע. If he said 'only a shekel', they get only a shekel. The ברייתא then begins the case of 'if they die'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Where do I get this from? From a ברייתא. A person says, 'Give my children a shekel every week.' If they really need a סלע (double that), the caretaker gives them a סלע. But if the father said, 'Give them only a shekel,' they get only a shekel. And if he said, 'If they die...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is starting to bring a source to back up his view from step 14. He quotes the opening cases of a ברייתא, and the case his proof depends on is just beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two cases show that we read a person's words by what he really meant. Plain 'a shekel' means 'whatever they need', while 'only a shekel' sets a firm limit. These cases set up the next clause, 'if they die', which is where רב ששת's proof will come from.

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not in the shekel and סלע cases. Those are background. The proof comes from the 'if they die' clause, which is only starting here.
